g.text: VI. Fictitious capital — paper claims on future surplus value
I. Real capital still produces surplus value
II. Capitalisation (how a title gets a price)
circuit : M - C … P … C' - M'
the only capital that produces s
raises funds once by issuing titles
price = expected income / rate of interest
as if it were interest on a principal
the money has already been spent
(or from wages — still not new value)
market in titles, not in factories
price difference on resale of a title
bursts when claims cannot be validated
rejected claim: the title is a second
Money does not exist twice (Capital III, ch. 29)
The sum advanced to an enterprise exists
as real capital in production. The share
is only a title to a corresponding portion
of the surplus value to be realised.
A rise or fall in the paper's price,
independent of that real capital, leaves
the wealth of the nation unchanged.
Doubly fictitious: the state has spent
the bond is a capitalised claim on future
tax, itself a share of surplus value.
The credit system that finances industry
also finances the market in titles.
the mediation of the production process"
